summary: After a complete frame, if exactly 1 byte of the next length prefix is buffered and the previous frame was over 16 bytes, the stale _dataSize takes the rewind branch: Position -= 2 lands inside the previous ciphertext and the stream desynchronises. evidence so far: Read in code; wire-protocol.md: one packet may span segments. Existing TestDecryptPcap85SplitPacket does not state this split. Effect on a client not yet known; the session's later C2S packets decode as garbage on the server.
proof method: xunit: PacketFactory.Read with two frames split after byte 1 of the second length prefix; expect 2 packets. Real frame bytes from a non-account capture.
risk if changed: Low: reset _dataSize after a full frame. CLI uses the same Read, so annotated dumps can only gain packets.

summary: Padding is 16 - pos%16, so an aligned packet gets a whole extra 16-byte block (1 to 16 bytes). Official captures show 0 to 15 (packet-wire-format.md, 753 files). WriteDataWithLengthPrefix:72-80 pads correctly.

summary: Size check ignores padding, so a body of 65511 to 65524 bytes reaches the checked (ushort) cast at :183 and throws (caught at Client.cs:159). summary: Client.Send and PacketFactory.Write take no lock; _t8Encrypt is scratch memory written by every Camellia round (Camellia.cs:472-500) and _packetCount++ is not atomic. Two threads sending to one client can corrupt a frame's ciphertext or reuse a counter. Other threads exist: PingRequestPacketHandler timer:24-36. OrderingLaneCount defaults to 1 (ServerSetting.cs:53), so handlers alone do not race at the default; more lanes are configurable.
evidence so far: Read in code. Likelihood at the default inferred: rare. Effect on a client not known.
proof method: xunit: two threads Write 10k packets on one PacketFactory, decrypt each frame, compare. A failing run proves it; a passing run proves nothing.
risk if changed: Low if a lock wraps Write plus SendRaw; order of frames must stay the order of counters. Lock contention on broadcast is small.
